Behavioral economics research labels this pattern
“signaling mismatch, where observable signals like follower composition convey information that diverges from stated identity. Census linked platform studies show that men in service industries such as beauty and wellness maintain female majority follower bases at rates 2.3 times higher than peers in construction or logistics. A 2022 analysis of 12,000 Instagram accounts found that follower gender ratios predicted occupational category with 71 percent accuracy, even when profile bios listed unrelated job titles. The same dataset revealed that audiences self sort by aesthetic content regardless of the creator’s gender presentation, creating clusters where demographic expectations break down. This sorting happens because visual content triggers category based attention more reliably than textual self description.

Which follower ratio surprised you most?
